page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing users to attach high-performance external block storage.

Performance benchmarks place the D32s_v4 in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks. The single-core stress-ng score is 1477.49, while the multi-core score reaches 29831.05. Memory performance is a notable strength, with a Passmark memory score of 2845.98, categorized in the top 25%. Large block memory bandwidth reaches 108.56 GB/sec for read-only operations and 47.26 GB/sec for write operations. In application-specific benchmarks, the server handles 26.08 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 20.31 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs include the complete lack of local NVMe storage and the absence of GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for heavy graphics processing or large-scale machine learning. For instance, LLM inference on a 70B model is weak at 5.64 tokens/sec for prompt processing, and text generation data is unavailable. However, the instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 22395.0, database operations, web serving, and moderate multi-threaded decompression tasks.
